## Maintainer clarification: full language support and CSTs by default are required The maintainer has clarified the acceptance scope: > There should be no limitations. Meta language must fully support representation and transformation of all the requested languages, and all the existing languages as CST by default. Treat this as a required correction to PR #196's intermediate scope. Full support for JavaScript, Rust, Rocq/Coq and Lean remains required, and **full concrete syntax trees must be the default representation for all existing languages**. The current four-language lexical subset, unavailable capability reports and unsupported translation descriptors do not fulfill that request. Complete the implementation in this PR; do not resolve the requirement by documenting the missing features as permanent exclusions. ### 1. Default CST support must cover the complete language inventory - [ ] Build one authoritative, versioned language/grammar inventory shared by both runtime packages. Reconcile it with every parser dispatch, alias, extension, advertised language, dialect, grammar importer, embedded-language target and conformance fixture. The current inventory is a minimum coverage audit, not permission to limit the maintainer's “all existing languages” requirement to four languages or a frozen shortlist. - [ ] For every language, the ordinary parse API must select its real grammar and construct a complete, lossless CST as links by default. Preserve grammatical node kinds, named fields, child order, all tokens/trivia/comments, exact source spans, error and missing nodes, and embedded-language boundaries. A root node around characters or delimiter groups is not a complete CST. - [ ] Supply default grammars and extension infrastructure that can express the full language syntax, including context-sensitive/project-defined notation, macros, dialects and embedded regions. Where parsing needs a project, imports or syntax extensions, accept and resolve that context rather than permanently declaring the construct opaque. Preserve surface syntax alongside expansion/elaboration and trace their relationship. - [ ] Provide equivalent default capabilities in JavaScript and Rust. Reuse mature grammars and common parser implementations/artifacts where practical. Lowering the advertised parity contract to the weaker scanner does not satisfy the full-CST requirement. - [ ] Keep missing grammars or unimplemented constructs visibly incomplete until implemented. A generic byte/text representation is useful storage, but must not satisfy a language's CST coverage gate. Do not remove a language, alias or construct from the inventory to make CI green. At head `c1ec894bff736677537810d701111c06069d003a`, the [Rust dispatcher](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/c1ec894bff736677537810d701111c06069d003a/rust/src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs#L141) already names Python, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Visual Basic, Delphi/Object Pascal, Rust, Go, R, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Perl, eight SQL dialect profiles, HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML/DTD, INI, Protocol Buffers and GraphQL. Other paths add Lean/Rocq, LiNo, CSV, JSON5, markup and embedded regions. Audit the [target registries](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/c1ec894bff736677537810d701111c06069d003a/rust/src/parity.rs#L572), natural-language and document representations too; retain their own meaningful syntax structures and do not silently drop them from the broader inventory. I reproduced the default-path gap in the PR's JavaScript package: | Input language | Example | Syntax links returned | |---|---|---:| | Python | `def f(x):\n return x + 1\n` | 0 | | TypeScript | `const x: number = 1;` | 0 | | Java | `class Main {}` | 0 | | Go | `package main\nfunc main() {}` | 0 | | JSON | `{"x":1}` | 0 | | HTML | `

Hello

` | 0 | All six inputs round-trip as text. That confirms preservation but does not establish the CST support requested here. ### 2. Full representation and transformation for the four requested languages - [ ] Cover the entire syntax and structured representation of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq and Lean, including imports/modules, scopes/bindings, recursive definitions, types/universes, effects, attributes, macros/notation, proof terms and tactics. Track grammar/version/edition coverage with executable evidence. A version string in a capability object is not proof of conformance to that language version. - [ ] Provide structure-aware query, insert, delete, replace, move, clone and construction of syntax; support generation from newly constructed or transformed networks, without relying on an untouched original source buffer. Update structure, spans, source mappings and diagnostics after edits, and verify emitted code reparses into the intended structure. - [ ] Implement binding-aware rename and transformations that preserve the intended meaning, including nested scopes, shadowing, capture avoidance, qualified/module names, macros and proof binders. Syntax-only transformations must identify their scope; do not label spelling substitution as semantic refactoring. - [ ] Keep genuinely shared language concepts reusable in meta-language and preserve language-specific distinctions and context explicitly. RML-specific syntax, foundations and proof authority remain in RML; their representation must use the full upstream infrastructure. - [ ] Preserve the existing requirement for all 12 directed translations among the four languages, with actual implementations, faithful encodings/runtime support where necessary, source mappings and behavioral/type/proof-preservation evidence. `UnsupportedObligation` is an honest report of unfinished work, not a completed translation implementation. CST availability alone does not complete translation. The lexical implementation still fails ordinary JavaScript cases. I ran these against this PR, in addition to the original fixed string/comment regression: ```text Rename identifier x -> y: input: const x = 1; const re = /x/; x; actual: const y = 1; const re = /y/; y; error: the regular-expression literal was changed as though it were an identifier. input: const x = 1; const text = `value: ${x}`; actual: const y = 1; const text = `value: ${x}`; error: the expression reference inside the template literal was not changed. parse: const = ; actual: verifyFullMatch().isClean() === true error: a clean lexical scan is being exposed without a full grammatical validity check. ``` Correct these failures and add them to the shared regression corpus. Cover the equivalent language-specific cases, not only these strings. Error recovery should preserve invalid source and report grammar errors rather than presenting it as a valid program. ### 3. Evidence, release delivery and completion - [ ] Commit an atomic requirement/coverage ledger preserving issue #195 and this clarification. Map every language and construct to grammar, implementation, positive/negative tests and transformation evidence in both runtimes. Do not replace missing implementation with more declarations, capability enums or documentation. - [ ] Use upstream language conformance suites, grammar corpora and representative real projects in addition to small fixtures. Exercise malformed input, comments/literals/interpolation, Unicode, macros, modules, proof syntax, mixed-language files and sequences of edits. Verify real node kinds/fields and tree relationships; a root node and an exact text round trip are insufficient. - [ ] Test both runtimes against the same expected CST/semantic contracts. Where internal layouts differ, normalize them under an explicit faithful mapping; do not erase distinctions merely to pass parity. Test against native parsers/compilers/provers where relevant, keeping those checks distinct from RML's internal reasoning authority. - [ ] Install and test the actually published npm and Rust artifacts. Resolve the continuing npm distribution gap linked in [#171](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/171), and demonstrate downstream RML integration with the released capabilities. - [ ] Update the PR description and docs to preserve **full support as the delivery requirement**. Report current gaps honestly during development. The present 97 passing JS tests and green CI do not discharge missing grammar, semantic transformation or translation coverage. - [ ] Remove the trailing `Fixes #195` while required work remains incomplete. The body currently says the issue must remain open and then supplies a directive that would close it on merge. Do not close #195 or claim completion until the full requirements are implemented and verified; a documented “intermediate foundation” is not the requested final result. This clarification changes the acceptance target; it does not authorize claiming that the current implementation already has no limitations. Implement the missing capabilities, keep failures observable while doing so, and supply the evidence before marking the work complete.

## Required acceptance gate: executable verification of every requirement, with no coverage exemptions

The maintainer requests full verification of **all** requirements in tests, so missing implementation cannot be bypassed by a green but incomplete suite. This comment supplements, and does not narrow, [issue #195](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/195), the [full-support clarification](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5795832509), and the committed requirement ledger. Complete the requested implementation in this PR; an intermediate subset or a promise of follow-up work is not acceptance.

### Verified baseline — not completion

At `dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857`, I independently reran `npm test` (102/102 passing) and `npm run check:parity`. The regex, template-interpolation, invalid-syntax, and zero-width-missing-node regressions pass. That progress is real.

However:

- The [inventory/ledger](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857/docs/issue-195-requirement-ledger.md) reports only 43/57 grammar-backed targets in JavaScript and 39/57 in Rust, with other required paths still specialized, lexical, or text-only. These counts include formats and profiles; they are not proof of full language conformance.
- The [inventory test](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857/js/tests/four-language-conformance.test.js) filters to rows already marked `grammar-cst`. Consequently, a missing grammar can remain outside that positive test while CI passes. Test the entire required inventory, not only its implemented subset.
- The same test file explicitly expects unavailable binding/type resolution and expects all 12 translation contracts to be unsupported. Such tests can verify truthful diagnostics, but **cannot count as positive acceptance tests for the requested capabilities**.
- The [implementation](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857/js/src/language-support.js#L85) still declares unavailable resolution/elaboration and no registered translation encodings.
- GitHub currently reports `isDraft: false`, while the description/ledger say draft. The description still ends with `Fixes #195` despite saying the issue will remain open.

### 1. Make requirement traceability machine-checked

- [ ] Commit a machine-readable manifest of **atomic, stable requirement IDs**, preserving every requirement from the issue, its clarification, this comment, and the ledger. Include source permalink, language/version/edition/construct, runtime, implementation entry point, test IDs/fixtures, expected observable behavior, verification checkpoint, and evidence artifact. Split compound requirements so a passing parser test cannot conceal a missing semantic or transformation requirement.
- [ ] Reconcile this manifest automatically with every parser/target registry, advertised language, alias, extension, dialect, grammar importer, embedded-language path, and documentation claim. Fail on missing, duplicate, dangling, or untested entries. The 57-target inventory is a minimum audit, **not a cap on “all existing languages.”** Do not reduce scope by deleting or reclassifying targets or assertions.
- [ ] Generate the human-readable ledger and completion summary from the actual test results and manifest. Hand-edited `Complete` labels, capability enums, test filenames, or self-reported `grammar-cst` statuses are not execution evidence.
- [ ] Every applicable requirement must have positive behavioral coverage in **both JavaScript and Rust**, plus appropriate negative/recovery coverage. A claimed non-applicability needs an explicit technical rationale and maintainer acceptance; missing implementation is not non-applicability.

### 2. Add a mandatory full-requirements CI gate

- [ ] Add a dedicated aggregate acceptance check, running on the exact PR head/merge candidate and included in required merge checks. If configuring repository protection needs maintainer permission, report that explicitly; do not claim the gate is enforced until it is configured.
- [ ] The gate must fail for any required row at its checkpoint that is missing, open, partial, unsupported, unexecuted, skipped, TODO, marked `xfail`, filtered out, or represented only by a placeholder test. Proper negative tests asserting expected diagnostics are required; `xfail` execution of a missing positive capability is not acceptance. Keep diagnostic tests for unfinished paths, but do not let them satisfy delivery tests.
- [ ] All implementation and candidate-artifact verification belongs to the required pre-merge checkpoint. Only checks that inherently require a published release may have a separate mandatory release-delivery checkpoint. Keep those rows visibly pending and overall delivery incomplete until they pass; do not use staging to postpone any language, semantic, transformation, translation, or integration implementation. The release checkpoint must prevent declaring completion/closing the issue on publication or verification failure.
- [ ] No `continue-on-error`, swallowed assertion failures, empty test selection, missing compiler treated as success, optional/manual-only acceptance jobs, capability-based filtering, or parity exemptions for required behavior. Shards are acceptable only if the aggregate verifies the complete expected set actually executed. A cancelled or missing job is not a pass.
- [ ] Test discovery and result ingestion must validate stable test IDs, fixture/corpus identity, and nonzero expected coverage for every matrix cell. Publish a per-requirement report with commit SHA, commands, toolchain/grammar versions, corpus revisions, results, and reproducible failure logs. A global test count or line-coverage percentage is not requirement coverage.
- [ ] Preserve the gate and its baseline. Changes that remove requirements, tests, corpus cases, assertions, or required checks must be surfaced as scope changes requiring explicit maintainer approval, not ordinary ways to restore green CI.

### 3. Minimum behavioral acceptance matrix

Each row below needs concrete assertions, shared fixtures in both runtimes, and failure cases where applicable. This matrix supplements the atomic manifest; it does not replace any earlier requirement.

| Area | Required executable evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Default CST for every required language/path | Call the normal public parse API, without a special opt-in registry to hide missing defaults. Assert actual grammar nodes, hierarchy, named fields, child order, tokens/comments/trivia, exact UTF-8 spans, error/missing nodes, and embedded-language boundaries against an independent expected structure. Assert exact reconstruction separately. A root plus text, a nonzero node count, or a delimiter/token tree is insufficient. Include all aliases, advertised extension dispatch, dialects, importers, document/natural-language representations, and embedded paths. |
| Complete four-language syntax | Inventory the constructs of JavaScript, Rust, Lean, and Rocq/Coq against their claimed versions/editions. Run applicable upstream conformance/grammar corpora and representative real projects, not one example per grammar. Include modules, attributes, recursive definitions, macros/token trees, scoped notation, proof terms/tactics, Unicode, malformed input, recovery, and mixed-language files. Explain the mapping from each external corpus to the capability it actually tests. |
| Project-aware representation | Load multi-file projects, imports, dependencies, plugins, dialect settings, macros and notation. Verify scopes/symbol identity, module references, recursive definitions, types, effects, universes, proof structure, and surface-to-expansion/elaboration traces. Missing project context must give accurate diagnostics, not fabricated semantic success. Supplying valid context must enable the required behavior. |
| Structured transformations and construction | Exercise query, insert, delete, replace, move, clone, and construction from scratch through public APIs. Test sequences of edits and serialize/reload boundaries; verify tree integrity, updated spans, provenance/source mappings, diagnostics, and emitted source reparsing to the intended structure. Discarding the original string while replaying unchanged retained tokens is not sufficient: newly constructed and structurally changed programs must work. |
| Binding-safe transformations | Assert which declarations and references change, not only output text. Cover shadowing, nested scopes, qualified/module names, Unicode, macro-generated names, Lean/Rocq binders, capture avoidance, and unaffected comments/strings/regex literals. Preserve the distinction between syntax-only replacement and semantic refactoring. |
| Shared concepts and language-specific distinctions | Test shared binding/typing/module/proof/provenance concepts without collapsing distinct effects, universes, or language semantics. Test schema versioning, capability/fidelity reports, extension registration, and the stable parse → links → transform → emit contract. Keep RML-specific foundations and proof authority downstream; demonstrate their use of the shared upstream representation. |
| JavaScript/Rust parity | Run the same corpus through both packages and compare normalized complete structures, fields, flags, spans, trivia, diagnostics, bindings, transformations, and translations. Define a faithful normalization; do not erase distinctions or lower both sides to text to obtain equality. |
| Validation and delivery | Validate emitted artifacts with the declared JavaScript host, `rustc`, Lean, and Rocq toolchains. Test clean package installation, public entry points, supported OS/runtime combinations, offline first parsing after installation, and downstream RML examples. Missing grammar downloads, undeclared local caches, source-checkout imports, and unpublished dependency pins must not be hidden. |

Keep the already-fixed JavaScript regressions permanently, and cover their language-specific equivalents. Add property-based/fuzz and metamorphic tests for round trips, malformed input, Unicode/spans, and edit sequences alongside independently specified examples. Self-consistency between a parser and its own emitter alone does not establish correctness.

### 4. Require successful translations for all 12 directed pairs

- [ ] JavaScript → Rust, Lean, Rocq.
- [ ] Rust → JavaScript, Lean, Rocq.
- [ ] Lean → JavaScript, Rust, Rocq.
- [ ] Rocq → JavaScript, Rust, Lean.

For **each pair in both runtime packages**, run the actual public translator on a construct/project coverage corpus, emit a real target artifact, parse and validate it with the target toolchain, and check the declared behavioral/type/proof-preservation contract. Cover nontrivial control flow, recursion, data/types, modules, effects, and proof-related constructs wherever applicable to the source; exercise explicit faithful encodings and their runtimes for constructs without direct target equivalents.

Record observation models, encodings, runtime dependencies, assumptions, provenance, and source mappings. Native compilation/kernel acceptance alone does not establish semantic preservation, and must not become RML's internal proof authority. Do not silently add axioms, weaken theorems, erase effects, relabel source text, or count a keyword demo as full translation. Tests asserting `UnsupportedObligation` remain diagnostic tests of unfinished work, **not acceptance of any translation pair**. Formal preservation obligations must remain explicit and be discharged where the contract requires proof.

### 5. Prove the acceptance tests detect the known shortcuts

- [ ] Add focused mutation/fault-injection checks showing that acceptance becomes red when a required parser is replaced with plain text or lexical fallback; a required inventory row/alias is removed; fields/trivia/spans are dropped; binding resolution is stubbed; rename ignores capture; an edit leaves stale structure; or a translator returns only an unsupported descriptor or relabelled input.
- [ ] Also demonstrate that skipping a required test/job or falsifying a capability/status declaration cannot produce a successful aggregate report. A passing suite that accepts these regressions is not an adequate acceptance gate.

### 6. Completion, packaging, and truthful status

- [ ] While implementation or pre-merge verification is unfinished, keep the PR genuinely draft. While any requirement, including publication verification, is unfinished, keep the issue open, synchronize the description and ledger, and remove `Fixes #195`/other closing directives. Do not label the work complete merely because general CI is green.
- [ ] Before merge, install and test the packed npm/crate artifacts from clean environments and exercise downstream RML against those exact candidate artifacts. Before claiming release delivery or closing the issue, install the actual published matching releases in clean consumers and run the same integration acceptance tests; record versions, integrity/checksums, and results. Keep publication-dependent requirements pending until that evidence exists—do not mark them passed because publication is planned. Resolve the distribution concern linked in #171.
- [ ] Provide a final requirement-by-requirement report linking implementation, executable tests, native validation, package evidence, and CI results, with **zero missing/open/partial required rows**. Any remaining gap blocks a claim of full delivery and must be reported plainly, not moved into exclusions or deferred outside this PR without explicit maintainer approval.

Finite testing does not mathematically prove arbitrary-program equivalence or support for an unbounded set of languages. That is a reason to combine complete requirement traceability, conformance evidence, extensible coverage, and explicit preservation proofs/contracts—not a permission to call a fixed shortlist universal or to waive missing functionality. The acceptance target remains the maintainer's full requested scope.

### 3. Mandatory working rules: resources, batching, cleanup

Automated sessions on this PR keep dying. The [latest one](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5953703216) was killed with **exit code 137** (out of memory) inside the Docker task container after several hours. The [maintainer already asked](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5940086274) for the following; it is now required:

1. **Work in bulk.** Draft a whole batch of related changes, commit, re-read the diff, then commit again. Push once the batch is complete; **CI is the full verifier.** Do not rebuild or re-test the whole project after each edit.
2. **Prefer JavaScript for experiments.** Prototype a grammar, executor, merge or translation change in `js/` first; it needs no compilation. Port the finished design to `rust/` in one batch, then run `cargo check` once.
3. **Run only targeted local checks**, with bounded parallelism:
   - JS: `node --test tests/<area>*.test.js` for the files you touched.
   - Rust: `cargo check --all-targets --all-features`, then `cargo test --test integration <filter>` or `--test unit <filter>`, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.
   - **Never run locally:** the full `acceptance:issue-195` pipeline, `run-issue-195-evidence.mjs`, the native Lean/Rocq/Rust toolchain matrix, clean-consumer installs, the RML/formal-ai workload clones, `cargo llvm-cov`, or upstream-corpus and whole-registry experiments. Those belong to CI.
4. **Fix `AGENTS.md`.** It currently says “Run the JavaScript checks (`npm test && npm run check`) and the Rust checks (… `cargo test --all-features`) before pushing.” That contradicts rule 3. Replace it with the targeted-check rule and a pointer to the CI jobs that do the full verification.
5. **Always be ready to clean up.** Run `node scripts/clean-caches.mjs` after every batch and before any long command. Remove `.issue-195-work/`, `issue-195-results/`, `issue-195-artifacts/`, cloned RML/formal-ai checkouts and their `target/` directories once a step is done. On a timeout or failure, kill leftover `cargo`, `rustc`, `node`, `lean`, `lake`, `coqc` and `rocq` processes before continuing. Commit early so an OOM kill loses nothing.

### 4. Split CI so a single failure is reported in minutes, not after the whole pipeline

Today one compile error costs 7 Rust jobs and a ~20-minute acceptance job, and it reports 255 false row failures. Change the workflows as follows, without weakening or removing any check:

- **Add a fast `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` gate (about 2 minutes).** Make Test, MSRV, Coverage, Fresh Merge and acceptance `needs:` it, so a compile error fails once, early.
- **Split test execution by category** into matrix jobs with their own 10–15-minute timeouts: Rust by target and filter (`--test unit`, and `--test integration` split into `grammar_*`, `inference_*`, and translation/conformance), and JS `node --test` by file group (grammar, translation, conformance/generative, downstream, tooling). Keep the existing check names, or add an aggregating job with the same name, so the required ruleset context stays valid.
- **Split the “Produce checkpoint evidence” step.** Today `run-issue-195-evidence.mjs` runs `suite-javascript`, `suite-rust`, every native translation pair for both runtimes, delivery packing and merge enforcement **sequentially in one step**, and it installs Lean, OCaml and Rocq even when Rust cannot build. Make these separate jobs: JS suite, Rust suite, native translations as a matrix by target language, delivery, merge enforcement. Each job uploads its own evidence artifact, and `Full Requirements Aggregate` only merges and evaluates them. If a suite cannot build, report it as **one gate error naming the suite**, not as 255 failing rows.
- **Add `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`** to every workflow. Head `8418ce50` alone started seven Issue 195 Full Acceptance runs.
- **Shrink the runtime-parity evidence.** The requirement report artifact is about 208 MB, and 188 MB of it is two 94 MB files: `issue-195-results/runtime-parity/{javascript,rust}.json`. Each holds the **complete serialized CST of every fixture**: 308 PDF-grammar trees of about 108 KB each (76 MB), 655 Links Notation grammar trees (12 MB) and 80 inventory trees (8 MB). `js/scripts/check-issue-195-runtime-parity.mjs` captures the Rust document through `execFileSync` with `maxBuffer: 512 * 1024 * 1024`, then runs `JSON.parse` on it. It also builds the JavaScript document in the same process and `stableJson`-stringifies both. That puts several copies of roughly 100 MB of trees in one Node heap at once. Record a stable digest per fixture and compare the digests; write the full trees **only for fixtures whose digests differ**. Stream results per fixture (for example, NDJSON) instead of building one giant string.

### 5. Memory and bottleneck audit of the code

A static review of `d2407c18` found no unbounded growth in the Rust `OnceLock` tables or the executor memo, which is capped by `memoLimit`. It did find these **unreasonable resource costs**. Fix each one and add a regression check where it can be measured, for example a bounded `--max-old-space-size` run or a peak-RSS assertion in CI.

1. **Uncapped parallel compile and test inside the evidence runner.** `js/scripts/run-issue-195-evidence.mjs:234-239` starts `npm test` **and** `cargo test --all-features` at the same time, in one `Promise.all`. `runCommand` (`:720`) passes `process.env` through unchanged, so there is no `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` or `RUST_TEST_THREADS` limit. `scripts/with-cache-cleanup.mjs` already sets those bounds, but this path does not use it. `--all-features` also compiles `lindera` with the embedded Jieba dictionary and `doublets`, on top of 57 `tree-sitter*` crates and 5 C grammars from `build.rs`. This is the most likely cause of the exit-137 kills, because agents follow `AGENTS.md` and run this locally. Run the suites sequentially, apply the bounded environment to every child process, and only enable the features that a requirement actually needs.
2. **All 60 WebAssembly grammars load eagerly at import time and are never freed.** `js/src/programming-language-parser.js:32-41` decompresses all 60 grammars and calls `Language.load` for each one in a module-level `Map` before anything is parsed. That is 7.6 MB of gzip, several times larger once decompressed, in the WASM heap of every process that imports the parser, including every `node --test` file process. Load each grammar on first use and cache it by ID.
3. **A new parser for every Markdown inline node.** `programming-language-parser.js:359` creates and deletes a `WebTreeSitterParser` for every `inline` or `pipe_table_cell` node. That means hundreds of WASM allocations for each large document. Reuse one parser, and still delete each tree.
4. **Per-character offset maps for every parse.** `sourceBoundaries` (`programming-language-parser.js:467-486`) builds a `Map` entry for **every character**, and `clipParsedSource` calls it twice (`:86`, `:118`). `utf8Input` (`:156-173`) keeps the text, its UTF-8 bytes and a complete UTF-16 byte string at the same time. On large Lean, Rocq or registry sources this is several times the input size per parse. Use sorted line or chunk checkpoints with binary search, and decode bytes in the `read` callback as they are needed.
5. **The runtime-parity evidence serializes everything** (see section 4): about 94 MB per runtime, read through a 512 MB `maxBuffer` and parsed in one heap. Switch to per-fixture digests and full trees only for fixtures that differ.
6. **Cache cleanup only runs on commit and in CI teardown.** `scripts/clean-caches.mjs` runs from the pre-commit hook, the opt-in `with-cache-cleanup.mjs` wrapper and the CI teardown. A long agent session that builds without committing never triggers it. Make `with-cache-cleanup.mjs` the documented way to run every local cargo or npm test command, and run it between batches.
7. **Native validation output stays on disk for the rest of the acceptance job.** `.rmeta`, `.olean` and `.vo` outputs under `issue-195-results/work/native/` remain until the final teardown, and some are uploaded. Delete them once each native cell is recorded.

### 2. Main focus: real, complete native Links Notation grammars for every catalog language

**Status today:**

**Catalog entries that still need a native grammar.** The 10 natural languages need a stated, tested treatment of their own, not a tree-sitter grammar.

- **Programming (37):** JavaScript, TypeScript, TSX, Rust, Python, C, C++, C#, Java, Visual Basic, Delphi/Object Pascal, Go, R, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Perl, Haskell, OCaml, OCaml Interface, Zig, Bash, Dart, Elixir, Elm, Erlang, Groovy, MATLAB, Nix, Odin, PowerShell, Solidity. - **Build (2):** CMake, Make.
- **Data (8):** HCL, YAML, TOML. Diff, JSON, INI, CSV and JSON5 are done, apart from recovery.

- **SQL (8):** ANSI, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, BigQuery, Snowflake.

**What “done” means for each language.** Every point is required, in both runtimes, with identical output:

1. A native `.lino` grammar that is the **output of the automatic merge pipeline** over all of the language's pinned sources: the official specification, ANTLR grammars-v4, tree-sitter and other mature grammars. Scale by importing (the ANTLR and tree-sitter-JSON importers already exist) and merging, not by hand-copying. Hand edits are recorded as reviewed merge decisions. This covers `MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE` and `MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED`.
2. **Error recovery in the native executor**: error and missing nodes, plus synchronization. Implement it **once, in the executor**, so all seven existing grammars become default parsers immediately. Then every new grammar ships as the default parser. This covers `GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES` and `GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`.
3. **External scanners represented natively**: indentation and layout for Python, Haskell, Lean, Nix, Elm, YAML and Make; heredocs; raw strings; nested comments; template literals; context-sensitive lexing. This uses the feature-union constructs (lexical modes and state). No foreign scanner code may stay on the production path.
4. A lossless CST by default: kinds, fields, order, exact tokens and trivia, spans, error and missing nodes, embedded-language boundaries. An optional AST with provenance. The tree reloads without the source, can be edited, and is emitted and re-parsed.

7. The catalog lists versions, dialects, aliases, extensions and embedded languages, and pins every grammar source with its license and provenance. This covers `GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`.

1. Executor recovery.
2. The four core languages: JavaScript with TypeScript and TSX, Rust, Lean and Rocq. Translation depends on them.
3. Family by family, so that shared concepts are designed once:

### 3. New requirement: the native grammars must use shared concepts

The meta-language library is real only if its grammars are written **in terms of shared concepts**. Then a construct that maps 1:1 in more than two languages is translated once, through its concept, instead of by a rule for every pair of languages.

**Today they are not.** For example, [`parity/grammars/native/json.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-195-cc10e17ab860/parity/grammars/native/json.lino) copies tree-sitter's node names (`_value`, `pair`, `object`) and has no reference to the concept records (`js/src/concept-records.js`, `parity/naming/canonical-concepts.json`). `json.lino`, `scheme.lino` and `racket.lino` contain no concept references at all. Scheme and Racket, and JSON and JSON5, were written independently, even though most of their constructs correspond 1:1.

**Required**, as new atomic ledger rows with JS and Rust tests:

- **Every rule of every native grammar maps to a canonical concept record.** It maps to a **shared** record when its meaning corresponds 1:1 in two or more languages, and to a language-specific record otherwise. Required distinctions stay intact (`I195-GRAMMAR-CONCEPT-DISTINCTIONS`): ordered vs unordered choice, integer and overflow models, binding rules, effects, universes. Concepts that look alike but differ are never merged.
- **Shared concept library.** Build it as the families above are merged, and add any concept that two or more grammars need. Examples:
  - literals: string, integer, floating-point, boolean, null;
  - identifier, line comment, block comment;
  - module, import, function definition, parameter list, call, block;
  - conditional, loop, assignment, binary and unary operation with an operator-precedence class;
  - class or record or structure, field;
  - list, array, map and object literals, key-value pair;
  - symbolic list (s-expression).
- **Tests:**
  1. A grammar test fails if any rule lacks a concept record.
  2. A per-language reuse report lists shared vs language-specific rules. It is published with `MERGE-QUALITY-EVIDENCE`.
  3. For every construct registered as 1:1 in three or more languages, an assertion checks that all of them resolve to **the same concept identity**. Examples: the JSON/JSON5 object and pair; Scheme/Racket list, symbol and boolean; function definition and call across JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Python and others.
  4. Negative fixtures prove that lookalike concepts stay distinct.
  5. A translation test proves that a construct shared by concept translates between two languages **with no pairwise rule**.
- **Names:**
  - Concept and rule names follow the readable-English naming rule: unabbreviated noun phrases for concepts, verb phrases for operations. `_value` and similar inherited names become English names; the original tree-sitter and ANTLR names are kept as aliases for reverse conversion.
  - Extend `npm run check:naming` to cover native grammar rule names and concept references.
